title: The Enum That Was Undefined: Naming a C++ Enum in QML, and the Integer It Accepted

questions.question: A C++ enum has no Q_ENUM_NS. What is its name in QML?
What is RobotMode.Fault in QML, when the C++ enum gives Fault the value 9?
questions.explanation: The values are the C++ values.

questions.question: A property holds a mode and QML assigns 99. What happens?
options: It is stored: nothing in QML stops it
questions.explanation: The stored value was 99, and its name is unknown.

questions.question: Where does the check that 99 is not a mode belong?
options: In the C++ that receives it, with is_valid_mode
questions.explanation: The meta object says unknown for 99.

questions.question: Why does mode_from_name refuse "auto"?
options: Names are exact: the case matters, and an interface that guesses is a risk
questions.explanation: auto, AUTO and Auto with a space were each refused.

questions.question: Why can a namespace have only one Q_NAMESPACE?
options: A namespace has one meta object, and a second Q_NAMESPACE would be another definition of it
questions.explanation: The lesson puts the enum in its own namespace.
